Work outside the purchased rung delivered anyway because saying yes was easier than routing it, so the fee stays the same while cost-to-serve rises and the precedent hardens; the one destination this practice never uses.

The shallow, evidence-backed read of an incoming prospect books taken at the sale - current, somewhat behind, materially behind, or unknown - which decides whether a monthly fee can be quoted at all and what catch-up the quote must assume.

The separately scoped, separately priced and separately accepted remediation of a defined historical period that brings a file from its incoming state to a reconciled, supported starting point; scoped at the sale as a distinct path and executed as the entry gate to the subscription, never absorbed into a monthly fee.

Telling a prospect that this subscription is not what they need - because their real need is a licensed professional, or because their volume genuinely suits software or hourly help - and referring them onward rather than selling into the gap.

An audit, review or compilation issued with a practitioner report, reserved to appropriately licensed professionals; named here only as a boundary class the practice never performs or implies, with the specific rules to be verified in the practice own jurisdiction.

The written record that must exist before a first subscription month or any credential is accepted: rung and scope, the counts and evidence that placed the client there, exclusions and their destinations, fee and rhythm, rung-move triggers, catch-up path, access terms, client responsibilities, the bookkeeping-side boundary statement and the exit terms.

A bounded, paid or time-boxed inspection of an incoming client ledger that establishes what state the books are in - last reconciled date per account, unsupported balances, residue accounts, subledger agings, payroll and loan support - and produces a severity-ranked findings register without remediating anything.

The dated trial balance the practice carries forward as the accepted starting point of its own work, recorded with its source, its accepted differences and every account labelled provided-not-verified, and retained unchanged as the baseline for everything after it.

The written, per-client set of coding decisions - recurring vendor to account, transfer versus revenue, principal and interest splits, owner-personal handling - each carrying the source of the decision, so coding is a rule being applied rather than a judgment re-made every month.

The one document per client that lets any qualified person in the practice run that client close without asking the usual preparer: systems and access paths, connection quirks, approved deviations, exceptions, contacts, packet composition and known landmines - and no credentials.

A transaction or balance that cannot be resolved by the practice alone because only the owner knows the fact or only a licensed professional may decide the treatment; it sits in a visible queue with the question in the owner language, a default treatment and an ask-by date.
A named ledger account where unresolved amounts sit visibly until the client or their licensed professional answers, used deliberately and reported as an explained balance rather than buried.

Agreeing a ledger account to the source statement or settlement report issued by the bank, card issuer, lender or payment processor rather than to the platform own feed balance, which is the only form of reconciliation this practice recognizes.

The set of evidence standing behind every balance-sheet line for a closed period: reconciliation reports, loan amortization schedules, fixed-asset additions and disposals, prepaid and deferred schedules, provider reports and subledger agings.

The deliberate sweep for the accounts where unexplained amounts accumulate - suspense, ask-my-accountant, undeposited funds, uncategorized - so that every flagged balance is either cleared or explained and disclosed before delivery.

The monthly deliverable sent to the owner: comparative profit and loss, balance sheet, cash position and a plain-language note page describing what changed and what remains open, written factually and containing no recommendation.

The software and procedural state that prevents a delivered period from being silently altered, together with the named path by which a genuine correction is authorized, made and reissued with a change note.

The standing three-way rule that the bookkeeper decides only what the rulebook already settles, the client decides facts only they know, and the licensed professional decides treatment - with lane, person, date, answer and form logged and the answer turned into a rule.

The practice own record of where recurring delivery time actually went per client per month, split at least into feed and reconciliation work, categorization judgment, client chasing, review and reporting, and unpriced goodwill.

The number of live subscription accounts one delivery seat can carry through a full close cycle at the promised turnaround and accuracy, derived from that seat available hours less non-delivery load and a stated reserve, divided by rung-weighted measured effort - always dated and always with a recheck condition.

A client monthly fee set against that client measured cost-to-serve for the same month under a written allocation rule, expressed as a mechanism rather than a target, with any shortfall tagged as behaviour, complexity or price.

The gradual entry of work into a live account that was never inside the tier the client bought - an extra entity, a new channel, a payroll run, a lender packet - detected against recorded scope-unit counts and named in the cycle it appears.

The announced schedule on which every account fee is compared against its measured scope and cost-to-serve, plus the named off-cycle triggers, disclosed to clients at engagement and executed with written notice ahead of any conversation.

The accumulated gap between what an early or long-standing client pays and what the same scope would be priced at today, created by years of small unpriced additions and skipped reviews, carried deliberately or repaid on a plan but never left invisible.

An observable behaviour that precedes cancellation with enough lead time to act - reports never opened, documents arriving later each month, the review call repeatedly rescheduled, payment slipping, or the relationship going quiet - checked on a cycle rather than noticed in hindsight.

The slide from explaining what the books show into recommending what the owner should do about tax, entity structure, financing or legal exposure; the specific way a bookkeeping practice crosses the licensed boundary, and the thing the boundary card and rehearsed stop-and-refer move exist to prevent.

The mechanism by which a seasonal client annual scope is priced as a level monthly subscription rather than a fee that collapses in quiet months, together with the alternatives of a genuinely reduced dormant tier or a pause with a stated capacity consequence, chosen in writing before the first quiet month.

The bundle handed to a departing client at exit: the ledger through the last closed period in a portable form, reconciliation status, the open-items list and where source documents live - delivered per the engagement terms and never withheld over a fee dispute.

The periodic meeting where the whole book is examined as a portfolio - seat load, contribution, drift and goodwill, price debt, risk register, admissions, exits and concentration - and where decisions that are individually easy to defer are actually made with an owner and a date.

competency_questions_covered: What exactly does this practice sell as a monthly subscription, and how do I tell whether a given request is inside it?
Where does bookkeeping stop and licensed-professional territory begin, and what do I say when a prospect asks me to cross that line?
What access to a client financial systems does each tier require, how is it granted, and what will the practice never accept?
Which niche should this practice serve, and how do I compare trades, e-commerce, restaurants and professional services without guessing?
Why does niching compound, what would prove it is compounding here, and what does concentration cost me?
Which countable facts about a prospect books decide the tier they belong in?
How is a fixed monthly fee arrived at honestly without copying anyone rate card, and how do I check the number after the first months?
What happens when a client outgrows the tier they bought, or asks for something outside it?
How do I answer a prospect who says an hourly bookkeeper is cheaper, or that their accounting software already does this?
Before I quote anything, how do I decide whether this prospect is a fit for a fixed-fee subscription at all?
When must I decline a prospect rather than sell to them, and how do I decline without leaving them stranded?
What selling behaviour will this practice not use, and what extra care does a frightened or unsophisticated owner get?
What must be written down and agreed before the first subscription month starts?
How would I know the offer itself is wrong, and what evidence forces a re-cut of the tiers?
What has to be true about a new client books before I promise them a monthly close, and how do I find that out without doing the cleanup for free?
How do I get into a client bank, ledger, processor and payroll systems without ever holding their passwords, and what do I do when the owner insists on messaging me one?
How far back should a cleanup go, and how do I set a starting balance I can defend when the prior records are unreliable?
How do I scope, price and agree a catch-up project as a separate gate so it never gets absorbed into the monthly subscription?
In what order do I actually perform cleanup work so that I do not redo months I have already touched?
What do I do with transactions only the owner can explain, and how do I keep chasing them from stalling the whole file?
When is a cleanup finished, and what must the client see and agree to before the subscription close cycle starts?
What exactly is on the monthly close checklist, in what order does it run, and what gate ends each step?
How do I know the numbers are actually right before a packet leaves the practice, and who checks the checker?
What goes into the monthly reporting packet, and how do I write the notes without giving advice I am not licensed to give?
What happens when a feed breaks, an integration changes, or the client goes silent and the month has to be closed with something missing?
How do I handle a correction to a period I already delivered and locked, and what does the client CPA get from me at year end?
How many live client accounts can one delivery seat carry at the promised close quality, and how do I know that number is measured rather than assumed?
Which clients in the current book are carrying themselves and which are being subsidised by the rest?
When must I stop admitting new subscription clients, and what happens to the demand I cannot serve this month?
How do I see unpriced work entering a live account before it becomes the new normal, and where does that work go once I have seen it?
When and how do I raise an existing client monthly fee without ambushing them and without trading on their fear of losing their books?
What do I do about long-standing clients still paying an old fee for a scope that has quietly grown for years?
How do I know whether the monthly reporting the client receives is actually read and used, and what do I change when it is not?
What belongs in the monthly review conversation, and at exactly what point must I stop and refer the owner to a licensed professional?
Which signals tell me a client is drifting toward cancellation, and which intervention matches which signal?
How do I handle a client whose business is in cash distress or who has stopped paying, without exploiting their situation and without subsidising them indefinitely?
How do I price and staff a client whose business runs hard for part of the year and goes quiet for the rest, without losing them in the dead months?
When is a client a mis-fit I should exit rather than keep saving, and how do I exit them without damaging their books or breaching confidentiality?
How do I build a steady referral flow from CPAs and niche communities without stepping on professional boundaries or leaking client information?
What does the periodic review of the whole book have to decide, and what evidence proves the practice is healthy rather than merely busy?
